deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is a working sheet for §12 ('Transformation') of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857), the section on birational transformation and moduli. The previous page sets up the notation. s is a single-valued function on the surface T with n poles, and s' another such function with n' poles. They satisfy an irreducible equation G(s,s')=0 whose degree in s is n' and whose degree in s' is n. The number of 'double points', where both take the same values at two places, is rho=(n-1)(n'-1)-p. Over the mathematics, part of the sheet carries a draft of a cover letter.

(1) Minimal pole number (first lines). Take a function with m poles at places eps_1..eps_m. It exists iff the p homogeneous linear equations sum_{mu} c_mu * phi_pi(eps_mu)=0 (pi=1..p) admit a non-trivial solution. Here phi_pi = C_pi(s,z)/(dF/ds) are the integrands of the p everywhere-finite integrals; on the page they appear as sum C(s_mu,z_mu) dz_mu/(dF/ds)(s_mu,z_mu).
- Equivalently, p+1-m of these equations must be consequences of the others. In modern terms this is the Riemann-Roch condition l(D)>=2, i.e. i(D)>=p+1-m.
- This imposes p+1-m conditions on the m places, leaving 2m-p-1 free parameters for the pole divisor.
- The divisors of a pencil already move in a 1-parameter family, so we need 2m-p-1>=1. Hence, 'generally speaking' (unless the branch values satisfy special conditions), the least pole number cannot be smaller than p/2+1.
- Explicitly: mu=(p+2)/2 for p even and mu=(p+3)/2 for p odd.

(2) Normal forms. 'Two quantities linked by an algebraic equation and forming a (2p+1)-fold connected domain can be expressed rationally in two variables sigma, sigma' such that':
- p=1: mu=2, G of degree (2,2), rho=0. Check: (2-1)(2-1)-1=0.
- p=2: mu=2, G of degree 3 in sigma and 2 in sigma', rho=0. Here sigma has 2 poles and sigma' has 3 poles. Check: (2-1)(3-1)-2=0.
- mu>2, p=2mu-3 (p odd): G of degree (mu,mu), rho=(mu-1)^2-p=(mu-2)^2.
- mu>2, p=2mu-2 (p even): G of degree (mu,mu), rho=(mu-1)^2-p=(mu-1)(mu-3).

(3) The case p=2mu-2. 'In the latter case', among the p linear homogeneous equations above, p+1-m must follow from the rest. That gives p+1-m conditions on the poles (s_1^0,z_1^0)...(s_m^0,z_m^0), leaving 2m-p-1 free. For m=mu=p/2+1 this is 1, so the pole divisors move only in the pencil itself. In modern terms there are finitely many minimal pencils.

(4) Moduli. The 3(p-1) constants can therefore be regarded as the moduli of a class of algebraic functions transformable into one another (birationally equivalent).
- A system of equally branched (2p+1)-fold connected algebraic functions depends on one arbitrary constant if p=1, and on 3(p-1) if p>1.
- My reconstruction of the standard count behind this: a function with n poles has w=2n+2p-2 branch points, by Riemann-Hurwitz. Subtract the 2n-p+1 constants of such a function to get 3p-3. For p=1 this gives 0, but the elliptic case has 1 modulus, which explains the separate p=1 clause.

(5) Abel's theorem, last lines. The differential equations sum_{mu=1}^{p+1} dw_pi^{(mu)}=0 (pi=1..p) are equivalent to (sum w_1, ..., sum w_p) ≡ (c_1,...,c_p) modulo periods, with constants c_pi. This is the integrated form used for the inversion problem.

(6) Overlaid letter draft. 'Hochgeehrter Herr Doctor! In der Hoffnung, daß Ew. Wohlgeboren die Veröffentlichung meiner Untersuchungen über Abel'sche Functionen durch Ihr vortreffliches Journal gestatten möchten, erlaube ich mir Ihnen beifolgend eine neue Darstellung der in meiner Doctordissertation [entwickelten Principien ...]'. This is almost certainly addressed to C.W. Borchardt, editor of Crelle's Journal, accompanying the 1857 Abelian functions memoir.
errors: No mathematical error in the final values. In the p=2mu-3 line, earlier attempts at rho were struck out; the surviving value (mu-2)^2 equals (mu-1)^2-(2mu-3) and is correct.

The claim that the minimal pole number is >= p/2+1 is stated 'allgemein zu reden', i.e. for generic branch values. Special (e.g. hyperelliptic) curves have smaller minimal pole number. Riemann flags the exception explicitly (special conditions among the branch values), so this is not an error.
The dimension count 2m-p-1 is a naive parameter count. It is justified generically (Brill-Noether, later proved by Griffiths-Harris 1980), but Riemann does not prove existence.

results.what: Lower bound and generic value of the minimal number of poles of a meromorphic function on a genus-p surface: p/2+1 (even p), (p+3)/2 (odd p), via counting p+1-m conditions on m poles
results.modern_name: Generic gonality floor((p+3)/2) (Brill-Noether count for g^1_d)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (count); Brill-Noether 1874; rigorous existence: Kempf / Kleiman-Laksov 1972-74; generic exactness: Griffiths-Harris 1980

results.what: Normal forms G(sigma^mu, sigma'^mu)=0 with double-point count rho=(mu-1)^2-p, giving (mu-2)^2 for p=2mu-3 and (mu-1)(mu-3) for p=2mu-2; special cases p=1,2
results.modern_name: Model of a curve in P1xP1 of bidegree (mu,mu); arithmetic genus minus geometric genus = number of nodes

results.what: Number of moduli: 1 for p=1, 3p-3 for p>1
Equivalence of sum dw_pi=0 with the congruence sum w_pi ≡ c_pi mod periods
Draft cover letter to the editor of Crelle's Journal (Borchardt) submitting the Abelian functions memoir as a new presentation of the principles of his dissertation

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is draft material for §12 of the published 1857 Abelian functions memoir: minimal pole number, the bidegree-(mu,mu) normal form with double-point count, and the 3p-3 moduli. All of it is well known as Riemann's. The only mildly notable item is the draft of the submission letter to Borchardt, which is of documentary interest.

checkable.asserts: With m=p/2+1 the pole divisor has exactly 2m-p-1=1 free parameter (just the pencil)
Branch points minus constants of an n-pole function gives 3p-3 moduli
For odd p=2mu-3, 2mu-p-1=2: a 1-parameter family of pencils, so two independent degree-mu functions can be chosen

transcription_corrections: The first case row reads 'Für p=1 ... mu=2. G(sigma^2, sigma'^2)=0, rho=0'; the deleted text begins 'Für p=1', not p=2.
In the line p=2mu-3 the rho value is (mu-2)^2; the material before it ('(mu-1)(mu-3)'-like) is struck out and should not be read as a factor.
In the linear equations the denominator is dF/ds evaluated at (s_mu,z_mu), i.e. sum_mu C_pi(s_mu,z_mu) dz_mu/(dF/ds)(s_mu,z_mu)=0 for pi=1..p, not 'dz_mu/dF'.
'enthält ... wenn p=1, von keiner' is likely 'von einer' (one modulus for p=1), with 3(p-1) for p>1; the sentence is a draft and partly struck.
'Hochgeehrter Herr Doctor! ... In der Hoffnung, daß Ew. Wohlgeboren ...' is a separate letter draft written across the mathematical text, not part of the derivation.
'Doctordissertation' line probably continues '... der in meiner Doctordissertation [entwickelten Principien]' — uncertain.
